issues: Subject clarity failed: intake does not define one clear manufactured object.
Abstract drift risk is elevated: intake does not sufficiently lock object-first behavior.
fixes: Set subject.type to a manufactured object class and name the exact object in subject.identity.
Add anti-drift rules and explicit bans on texture-only, atmosphere-first, and abstract-first outcomes.

revised_intake.creative_intent: Generate a clean matte B4C technical ceramic material study, applied to a clearly readable manufactured object, while strictly avoiding abstract, atmospheric, or texture-only outcomes.

must_have: clear, readable contour evidence of a manufactured object
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture
visible edge, rim, bevel, seam, or contour evidence
material visibly attached to the object

composition.framing: tight, focused on the material surface of the object

constraints: highlight material properties and texture without harsh shadows
ensure full readability of the object's form

core_risks: Drifting into abstract or atmospheric compositions
Losing the manufactured object's identity or form
Incorrect material read (e.g., glossy, soft, organic)
Generating a texture-only output without a clear subject
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Always force a clearly readable manufactured object as the subject.
Explicitly ban texture-only, atmosphere-first, abstract-first, and subject-loss outcomes.
Protect readable contour evidence of the engineered component.
Suppress any visual cues that suggest abstract forms or atmospheric effects over a concrete object.
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
do not allow abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first subject drift
keep material identity explicit and stable
success_criteria: Immediate recognition of a single, manufactured technical ceramic object.
Clean, matte B4C technical ceramic material read is dominant and accurate.
Material appears dry, dense, and engineered.
No visual ambiguity regarding the object's manufactured nature or the material's identity.
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
image does not read as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
revised_intake.direction_summary: Prioritize a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read on a clearly defined, dry, dense, engineered manufactured object, strictly avoiding abstract or texture-only interpretations.
